title: lightweight oncall profiler and noise-aware notification throttler
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Opt-in oncall profiler and noise-aware notification throttler to reduce pager fatigue; new metrics and config flags; safe rollout behind feature flag.
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight, opt-in oncall profiler that samples ephemeral runtime signals during active incidents and a noise-aware notification throttler that reduces bursty alerts while surfacing high-confidence playbook suggestions. Motivation: repeated noisy alert bursts during transient infra flapping are a major source of fatigue; diagnosing those incidents also requires a concise fingerprint. This change provides low-overhead incident fingerprints and a probabilistic throttling policy so teams can tune sensitivity per-service.

What changed:
- Introduced slo-toolkit/pkg/profiler: a sampler that records short-lived CPU/memory/thread/req-rate histograms and top-N span traces (via existing tracing hooks) only when an incident session is active and the profiler feature flag is enabled.
- Added a noise-aware notification throttler that groups similar alerts arriving in short windows and applies a bayesian noise model to suppress low-confidence duplicates while promoting alerts that match historical escape patterns.
- New configuration knobs (defaults.yaml) allow per-service sampling window, max-samples-per-hour, throttle thresholds, and a conservative safe-mode that always forwards critical alerts.
- Console/UI additions to visualize an incident fingerprint timeline and to view the profiler samples alongside suggested playbook steps.

Implementation notes:
- Profiler is designed to be extremely lightweight: sampling is adaptive (lowering frequency during CPU pressure) and stores at-most 3 ephemeral samples per incident by default. Captured artifacts are transient and only retained if an incident is marked for postmortem; otherwise they are garbage-collected within 24 hours (configurable).
- Notification throttler uses an offline-trained prior (policy store) plus an online estimator to compute suppression probability. By default it is conservative: suppression requires both a low posterior and a minimum burst-size.
- All collection is opt-in for private deployments. For hosted usage we expose a tenant-level feature flag and robust PII/PIA filters so samples do not include user data (see privacy section in docs).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated behind config flag and 'oncall_profiler: enabled=false' by default.
2) Initial internal rollout to SRE and 3 beta product teams for 2 weeks.
3) Gradual enablement with telemetry gates: CPU overhead < 1% P50, suppression recall impact < 0.5% false-suppress on P1s.

Testing and monitoring:
- Unit tests for sampler logic and throttler model; e2e harness simulates alert storms and validates no-regression for critical alerts.
- New metrics: slo_toolkit.oncall.profiler.samples_total, slo_toolkit.oncall.profiler.sample_overhead_ms, slo_toolkit.oncall.throttler.suppressed_total, slo_toolkit.oncall.throttler.false_suppress_rate.

Security & privacy:
- Samples are scrubbed via existing PII filters at collection time. The profiler honors tenant opt-out and obeys retention policies. Security scan performed and no secrets allowed in samples.

Related work: ENG-9482 (oncall tooling v2), SRE-3314 (noise modeling). Links: Linear ENG-9482.

review_comments: Tomás Ortega (reviewer): This looks promising. Two asks: 1) can we make the retention window explicit in the default config so legal can review? 2) I'm concerned about CPU overhead on small nodes — please include an opt-out at the service-level as well.

Aisha Kapoor (author): Added explicit retention setting to defaults.yaml and an instrumentation flag per-service. Sampler is adaptive and we added a pressure check that reduces sampling to zero under >80% CPU; documented in the implementation notes.

Maggie Lin (reviewer): Please add an easier way to opt into the profiler for internal teams without going through infra changes (a bootstrap flag or CLI). Also add an alert that fires if false_suppress_rate rises above 1%.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Added oncall-ctl bootstrap flag and the prometheus alert; updated e2e test to assert suppressor recall under synthetic storms.
Ravi Menon (approver): Verified metric names and that the security scan passes. Approving, please squash-merge once CI is green.
